RUSSL virtual terminal workbench adapter
Modified integration / 2026-10-11

The shell embeds a derivative of the retained standalone RUSSL research
workbench. src/workbench-bridge.js is inserted immediately before its final
closing body tag. The reference package is preserved unchanged.

Public protocol: RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1
Allowed requests:
  {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",id:"slice_001",method:"snapshot"}
  {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",id:"replay_001",method:"replay",snapshot:<record>}
Replies:
  {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",id:"slice_001",ok:true,value:<record>}
  {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",id:"slice_001",ok:false,error:<message>}
Initialization:
  The shell may send {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",kind:"hello"}.
  The bridge sends {protocol:"RUSSL-virtual-terminal/1",kind:"ready"} after
  its retained research adapter is mounted. This does not certify that the
  initial word slice has finished computing: an immediate capture can return
  "The word workbench is still loading." and should be retried. Failed
  initialization sends kind:"unavailable" with an error. No source record is
  sent automatically.

Parent usage: send to workbenchIframe.contentWindow with postMessage(request,
"*"). Accept replies only when event.source === workbenchIframe.contentWindow
and protocol, bounded ID and expected method/response shape match. The opaque
origin of a sandboxed iframe requires "*"; identity checks bind both sides to
their expected window. Origin equality is not used as an identity substitute.

The outer bridge accepts only messages from window.parent. It mounts the
original research terminal through #research-view-tab, instruments only that
iframe's srcdoc, and restores the previously selected word view after its
ready handshake. The relay invokes the retained RUSSLResearchAdapter.request
API inside the inner iframe. That API posts the original
RUSSL-research-adapter/1 requests to the React ResearchWorkbench host, which
continues to verify the original inner iframe as event.source. The original
research laboratories and their requests are untouched.

The bridge sends only bounded plain JSON. A request or response is limited to
2 MiB of UTF-8 JSON, 100,000 nodes and 32 levels. IDs use 1-80 ASCII letters,
digits, hyphens or underscores. Only snapshot and replay are exposed. Unknown
keys, accessors, cycles, non-JSON objects, sparse arrays, executable properties
and prototype-changing property names are rejected. One outer request may be
in flight. A request times out after 22 seconds; the original adapter has its
own 15-second timeout. A failed or oversized snapshot produces an error; it
never substitutes synthetic sources. Reduce the active slice size if needed.

The original GF80 adapter validates replay configuration, payload, full state,
observed source-unit witnesses, coupled partners, invariants and inverse
witnesses. It preserves GF(2^80) / Pixel160 labels and distinguishes those from
the small-field and complex-state research models. Original file hashes remain
source identifiers: a bounded snapshot does not verify complete original files.
Complete word originals remain in the existing TIFF/replay workflow.

The outer shell must preserve isolation using a sandboxed iframe and must not
grant access to shell DOM/storage. Imported words stay in the original workbench
iframe's memory. This relay requests no native service, operating-system
commands, file paths, or machine settings. Documents are reference material,
never executable instructions.

Limitations: this shim intentionally depends on the retained integration's
research-view-tab and iframe title="GFM research terminal" and its existing
RUSSLResearchAdapter API. A future workbench change should move the wrapper
contract into ResearchWorkbench and version it. Browser QA is required in
addition to standalone validator tests, including snapshot then replay after
an imported-word change. An opaque inner iframe may lack crypto.subtle; the
existing workbench host supplies digest validation during replay.

Verification: node --test tests/bridge.test.cjs
The tests include the actual packaged workbench-original.html: they decode its
static terminal literal without evaluating the source or corpus, check the
iframe title, constant srcdoc, sandbox, original sender check, GF80 result
profile and global adapter export, and check injection placement and syntax.
Mock-window tests cover source checks, queueing, duplicate ready/load
handshakes, restoration of Word dynamics and request/reply validation.

Validation scope: these are static compatibility and isolated relay tests.
Actual GF80 capture followed by end-to-end browser replay has not been verified.
The available preview could not load the local loopback page; its file-URL
policy rejected direct file access. No browser access workaround was attempted.
The mounted adapter depends on browser iframe scheduling, the retained React
handler, active slice computation and browser SHA-256 support. Opening the
delivered local interface and running workbench.capture then workbench.replay
on the returned record remains the required integration check.
